request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (30,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 30.8% (95% band 28.9% to 32.4%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= -1: -0.1; 0: -0.6; 1: +0.7; >= 2: +2.4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.63, 95% band [+2.43, +2.80]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 15.0% (95% band 13.2% to 16.9%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 74999: +0.5; 75000-144999: 0; 145000-304999: -0.3; >= 305000: -0.5 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.07, 95% band [-1.17, -0.89]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 9.2% (95% band 5.7% to 10.9%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 10447: -0.3; >= 10448: +0.09 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.73, 95% band [+0.43, +0.89]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 6.2% (95% band 4.7% to 8.1%); rank 3 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1222: +0.149; >= 1223: -0.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.47, 95% band [-0.68, -0.30]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 2.5% (95% band 1.5% to 4.1%); rank 5 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 4: 0; >= 5: -1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.13, 95% band [-0.01, +0.27]).
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 2.5% (95% band 1.9% to 3.9%); rank 5 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.25 (95% band [+0.09, +0.43]) from x = 23 (5th percentile) to x = 53 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.3% (95% band 1.0% to 4.4%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.12 (95% band [-0.28, -0.03]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 19,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.2% (95% band 0.9% to 4.1%); rank 5 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.10, 95% band [-0.31, +0.17]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 0.2% (95% band 0.2% to 1.5%); rank 8 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.01, 95% band [-0.07, +0.14]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 19.5% (95% band 16.5% to 19.9%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.26 (95% band +1.15 to +1.48) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +6.91 (95% band +6.05 to +6.99) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: -0.81 (95% band -1.02 to -0.51) when `PAY_0` = -2, +4.85 (95% band +3.91 to +4.91) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 4.4% (95% band 3.7% to 5.4%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +1.36 (95% band +0.82 to +1.85) when `AGE` = 23, +0.15 (95% band -0.24 to +0.35) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.71 (95% band +0.35 to +0.99) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.50 (95% band -1.20 to -0.08) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 2.2% (95% band 1.7% to 3.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.55 (95% band -0.72 to -0.35) when `EDUCATION` = 1, -0.72 (95% band -1.05 to -0.57) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.27 (95% band +0.15 to +0.47) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.10 (95% band -0.16 to +0.30) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `AGE & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 1.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.8%).
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: -0.04 (95% band -0.40 to +0.35) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, +0.14 (95% band -0.28 to +0.71) when `BILL_AMT2` = 195,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 195,000: -0.17 (95% band -0.89 to +0.23) when `AGE` = 23, +0.00 (95% band -0.33 to +0.27) when `AGE` = 53.
- `BILL_AMT1 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.0% to 2.2%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.81 (95% band +0.45 to +0.96) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +0.47 (95% band +0.17 to +0.84) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.35 (95% band +0.03 to +0.52) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +0.01 (95% band -0.18 to +0.25) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The biggest driver of predicted default is the most recent repayment status (PAY_0): applicants who were paid up or only one month behind carry little extra risk, while those two or more months behind carry a much higher predicted risk, with the change from the 5th to the 95th percentile worth about 2.6 units on the log-odds scale."},{"id":2,"text":"The second driver is the amount of credit granted (LIMIT_BAL): larger limits are associated with lower predicted risk, with a net change of about -1.1 across the typical range, although this effect is clearly smaller than that of repayment status."},{"id":3,"text":"The most recent bill amount (BILL_AMT1) and the most recent payment amount (PAY_AMT1) matter moderately: higher bills raise predicted risk and larger payments lower it, but each effect is roughly a third or less of the repayment-status effect."},{"id":4,"text":"Repayment status and education interact strongly: the penalty for being behind on payments is far larger for applicants with high school education than for graduate-school applicants, so education changes how much a payment delay matters rather than acting as a separate driver on its own."},{"id":5,"text":"Age and bill amount also interact: the bill amount has a large effect for younger applicants but little effect for older ones, and age itself has only a small, uncertain effect on its own."},{"id":6,"text":"Education, age, the earlier payment and bill amounts from August and July, and the other interactions contribute little to the predictions, and their intervals are wide enough that their direction is not firmly established."},{"id":7,"text":"The data do not settle the precise shape of the age and earlier-month effects between their extreme values, so these should not be read as firm patterns in the model."}]}
